Simulate single-arm cohorts with correlated endpoints and an adverse event

Source: R/SimCohorts.R
SimCohorts.Rd

Generates patient-level data of several single-arm cohorts for many simulated trials: progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and objective response, correlated within a patient, from the CorOncoEndpoints package, and a binary adverse event that is independent of the other endpoints. The data can be cut at a common calendar time of analysis.

Usage

SimCohorts(
  nsim,
  n,
  arms,
  ae.rate,
  cutoff = NULL,
  a.time = NULL,
  a.rate = NULL,
  a.prop = NULL,
  d.hazard = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

nsim

Number of simulated trials.

n

Integer vector of cohort sizes, one per cohort.

arms

A list of OncoArm objects, one per cohort (or a single object). The names of the list are the cohort labels; unnamed cohorts are labeled "Cohort1", "Cohort2", and so on.

ae.rate

Numeric vector with the probability of the adverse event in each cohort.

cutoff

Calendar time of the analysis, or NULL for no cutoff.

a.time, a.rate, a.prop

Accrual of each cohort, passed to rOncoEndpoints: NULL, a numeric vector used for every cohort, or a list with one vector per cohort.

d.hazard

Hazard of an exponential dropout time, a scalar or one value per cohort.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A data frame with one row per patient, ordered by sim and cohort, with columns sim, group, accrual_time, pfs_tte, pfs_event, os_tte, os_event, response (observed by the cutoff when cutoff is given) and ae.

Details

Each cohort is described by an OncoArm object of the CorOncoEndpoints package (see OncoArm), which specifies the PFS median, the response rate, the association between PFS and response and the OS model. The cohorts are generated independently by rOncoEndpoints, one call per cohort, so that each cohort can have its own accrual and dropout. With seed, cohort j uses stream j of the random number generator seeded with seed, and the results are reproducible.

The adverse event of each patient is a Bernoulli variable with probability ae.rate of the cohort, independent of PFS, OS and response, and is taken as known at the analysis for every enrolled patient.

With cutoff, the data are restricted to patients enrolled before the calendar time cutoff (on the time scale of a.time, which starts at 0), and PFS and OS are censored at the cutoff by CutoffData; a response counts only if it was observed before the cutoff. Accrual intervals that start later than 0 (for example a.time = list(c(0, 12), c(6, 18))) describe cohorts enrolled at different times.

See also

SimSelection

Examples

arms <- list(
  Cohort1 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 8, orr = 0.45, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 18),
  Cohort2 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.30, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 15))
d <- SimCohorts(nsim = 2, n = c(30, 30), arms = arms, ae.rate = c(0.35, 0.20),
                cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = 1)
head(d)
#>   sim   group accrual_time   pfs_tte pfs_event    os_tte os_event response ae
#> 1   1 Cohort1    4.4648115 19.535189         0 19.535189        0        1  1
#> 2   1 Cohort1    9.9596607 10.103116         1 10.103116        1        1  1
#> 3   1 Cohort1    5.9214897  1.476153         1  4.644088        1        0  0
#> 4   1 Cohort1   11.8327362  5.596166         1  5.596166        1        1  1
#> 5   1 Cohort1    6.0778319  3.599755         1  3.599755        1        0  0
#> 6   1 Cohort1    0.5534634 10.252275         1 11.920372        1        1  0
table(d$sim, d$group)
#>    
#>     Cohort1 Cohort2
#>   1      30      30
#>   2      30      30
